###chapter 1
"Look, Lyra. Twenty years. That’s how long we took care of you. We’ve been way too generous, honestly." Arthur slid a heavy stack of documents across the mahogany. "Just sign the damn papers."

A check followed the paperwork. Five hundred grand. "Call it a parting gift," he muttered, tapping the paper. "A little thank-you from the Wynns for the memories."

Lyra just stood there. The room smelled like expensive, soothing incense, but she wasn't buying the vibe. Her dark eyes flashed with pure, unadulterated mockery.

"Five hundred grand?" A sharp, nasty little smirk tugged at her lips. "Am I really that cheap to you guys? Or... wait. Is half a mil literally all a 'high-society' family like the Wynns can scrape up these days?"

Three months. That’s how long ago the DNA test blew their lives up. Lyra wasn't theirs. So, they threw millions into a frantic manhunt to find their real kid—Willow.

And boom. The golden child was back.

Meanwhile, Lyra—the girl they dumped in some backwater town as a kid and only dragged back four years ago—was suddenly garbage. Ready for the bin.

"Excuse me? Five hundred thousand isn't enough?" Eleanor sneered, her face twisting in pure disgust. "Your redneck parents couldn't make that in a lifetime of breaking their backs. And you're complaining? Sign the damn thing! Sign it, and we are done. You walk, we walk. Total strangers."

"Oh, Mom, don't be like that..." God, money really does a number on people. Genevieve had been back for all of two months, but she was already dripping in custom designer threads and blinding jewelry. She looked the part. Total trust-fund princess.

She put on this sugary-sweet face, her voice dripping with fake sympathy. "I mean, she’s been living the glam life for twenty years. Of course she’s terrified of going back to the sticks."

Genevieve knew the gossip. Lyra’s real family was straight-up trailer trash. A dying, bedridden grandpa. A deadbeat, jobless dad. Three brothers so broke they couldn't even dream of getting married.

Talk about parasites. The second Lyra set foot in that house, they’d probably auction her off to the highest bidder for quick cash.

Genevieve practically vibrated with smug satisfaction. She dragged out the word *countryside*, staring hard at Lyra, waiting for her to break.

But Lyra just stood there, the afternoon sun hitting her face, making her look ridiculously, effortlessly gorgeous. Genevieve’s eyes flared with instant, ugly jealousy.

Her fake smile stretched wider, her voice turning cloyingly sweet. "I mean, sure, they live in the literal slums... but hey, they're your *real* family. Better than staying here and walking on eggshells, right?"

She spat out *real family* like a victory lap. A total, petty dig.

It was so pathetic Lyra actually laughed out loud. She locked her icy gaze onto Genevieve. "Did you spend so much time in the gutter that you forgot how to act civilized the second you got some cash?"

She curled her lip, a brutal smirk forming. "Then again... you *are* their kid. Makes sense."

Boom. Direct hit to the parents, too. Beverly’s eyes went wide with fury. She slammed her palms onto the desk, scraping her chair back as she stood up.

But before she could even scream... Lyra’s voice cut through the air like a knife. "I'll sign."

Beverly choked on her own rage.

Lyra grabbed the pen. She didn't even look at the fine print. She flipped straight to the back page, pressing the tip right onto the dotted line. Fast. Sharp. No hesitation.

She scribbled *Lyra* in bold, aggressive strokes. Zero regrets. Zero doubts. Just pure, cold finality.

Done. She flicked her wrist, tossing the pen onto the desk. It clattered against the wood.

Then, her pale fingers drifted over to the half-million-dollar check. She tapped it. Once. Twice.

Beverly watched her, her lip curling in pure disgust. *Typical.* Bad blood is bad blood. A cheap little nobody who could be bought off for a quick buck.

But then... Lyra snatched the check. With a savage, lightning-fast flick of her wrist... The paper sliced through the air and slapped Wallace right across his smug face.

Her voice dropped to absolute zero. 

"Keep it. Consider it a down payment on the Wynn family's funerals."

###chapter 2
That check smacked Wallace right in the face. It was a giant, collective slap to every single Wynn in the room.

"Lyra!" Wallace ripped the paper off his skin, his face turning dark. He stared at her, totally thrown. Where was the quiet, pathetic girl who used to crawl around their feet like a stray begging for kibble? Who the hell was this?

Lyra didn't blink. Her eyes were dead cold. She spun on her heel and walked out, shoulders back, spine like steel. No looking back. She was done with this toxic family. 

God, she used to beg for their love. When they dragged her from the sticks, she’d spent every second kissing their asses, trying to fit in. She’d been lower than a beaten dog. She’d spent hours researching organic meal plans and custom essential oils just to get a cheap smile out of them. She’d even burned her own high-society contacts to clear the runway for Wallace’s social-climbing dreams. 

And what did she get? Constant nagging. Zero appreciation. Her desperate love was just a punchline to them. The second Genevieve showed up, they threw Lyra out like yesterday's garbage. That was the exact moment her heart died.

The heavy door clicked shut. 

A beat of dead silence. 

Then Beverly lost it. Her chest heaved, and she jabbed a finger at the door. "Oh, so she’s got an attitude now? Who does she think she is?"

Wallace glared at the crumpled check in his fist. The image of Lyra’s icy, confident exit burned in his mind. It felt heavy. "Shut up, Beverly!" he barked. "She signed the damn waiver. She’s gone. Drop it."

"Oh, so now I'm the bad guy?" Beverly shrieked, shaking with rage. "I did this for Genevieve! Who knows what kind of cash her hillbilly mother left her? She’s a nobody! Why should she get a dime of our family money? It makes me sick. My poor Genevieve suffered in the dirt for twenty years while that brat lived like royalty in her place!"

"Mom..." Genevieve squeezed Beverly’s arm, her eyes instantly watering. "I know you’re just looking out for me. But it’s my fault she has to..." She sniffled, a tear rolling down her cheek. "Mom, let me go say goodbye."

Beverly’s heart melted. "Ugh, you’re way too sweet for your own good."

Genevieve hurried out. Downstairs, Lyra was at the couch, unzipping a cheap canvas bag to grab her stuff.

"Lyra!" Genevieve ran up, putting on her best puppy-dog eyes. "Look, I’m so, so sorry. I just wanted my parents back. I swear I didn't mean to steal your life. I actually begged them to let you stay, but, well... they were just so worried I’d feel left out, so they kicked you out instead."

"Oh, and... Caspian." Genevieve smirked, making sure the maids couldn't see her face. Her eyes gleamed with pure malice. "Caspian wants a massive engagement bash in three months. He wants the whole city to know I’m his girl. I mean, I know you chased him for years, but... we're good, right? You don't hate me?"

Lyra’s hand froze on the zipper. She slowly looked up. Her eyes were completely blank. No anger, no pain—just pure, high-and-mighty disgust, like she was looking at a bug. 

She let out a cold, sharp laugh. "Honestly? Congrats," Lyra said, her voice dripping with ice. "You just dumpster-dived for the trash I couldn't wait to throw away."

###chapter 3
That one word—*trash*—instantly killed Genevieve’s smug grin. Her pretty face warped into a nasty scowl.

The way Lyra looked down her nose at her felt way worse than a screaming match.

It basically told Genevieve that the prize she’d clawed her way to get was just straight-up garbage.

"Yeah, that goes for the whole 'Miss Wynn' gig too," Lyra said. She scanned the ridiculously fancy room and let out a dry chuckle. "And, oh, Caspian. The guy you practically bent over backward to get into bed."

Her grin turned sharp. "Better hold onto them real tight, babe. Don't let go."

Genevieve went completely white. She clenched her jaw, her face twisting with pure, burning shame.

She wound up her hand to slap Lyra's face.

But then, out of the corner of her eye, she spotted someone. Instantly, she flipped the switch to victim mode. She stumbled back, hit the floor hard, and forced her eyes to well up. "Lyra, I just wanted to say sorry! Please don't hate Mom and Dad. Why would you do that...?"

"Lyra!"

Beverly stormed in right as her golden child hit the deck. Fuming, she lunged forward. "We put a roof over your head for years, and you have the nerve to shove my Genevieve?!"

Lyra just stood there, watching Beverly scoop Genevieve up like she was made of glass. It was almost funny.

The old Lyra would’ve lost her mind crying, begging to know why she wasn't good enough, why she was always second best.

Now? She felt absolutely zero.

"Perfect," Lyra muttered.

She reached into her beat-up tote and yanked out a red velvet box.

*Thud.*

It hit the floor right by Beverly’s designer shoes.

The lid snapped open, spilling out a cheap, ugly pearl necklace.

"Take your trash back."

Beverly had basically thrown that thing at her for her eighteenth birthday.

It was clearly some leftover junk she didn't want.

Back then, though, Lyra had treated it like a million bucks.

Now, she was totally over it.

Beverly stared down at the pearls, squinting. She couldn't even remember buying the damn thing, let alone giving it away.

Still, the disrespect hit her like a physical slap.

"What the hell is this, Lyra?" she shrieked. "You lived high on the hog for twenty years on Genevieve's dime! You don't get to be pissed off!"

"I was literally a newborn, lady. How is that on me?" Lyra scoffed. "And honestly, Eleanor, you couldn't even spot your own kid. Go get a brain scan. Seriously, stupidity might be genetic."

Beverly’s face went dark, her voice hitting a dog-whistle pitch. "You ungrateful little bitch! So the sweet act was all fake? Now that we're tossing you out, you show your real teeth, huh?!"

"You snake! Go back to the dirt where you belong and rot in poverty!"

"Don't you dare come crawling back to us!"

Lyra just stared. Her red lips curled into a cold, badass smirk that made her look totally in control.

A cold shiver hit Beverly's spine. Her screaming died instantly, and she took a couple of steps back without even realizing it.

Lyra’s grin widened. "Like I'd ever want to," she muttered, rolling her eyes.

"Excuse me? What the hell does that mean?!" Beverly lost her mind, screeching in pure shock.

"It means your precious Wynn name is absolute trash to me." Lyra smiled, her eyes dripping with pure contempt. "Or, let me dumb it down for you—you're an idiot."

###chapter 4
Beverly looked like she was about to pop a blood vessel. Her fancy-lady face went totally ugly, eyes burning with pure rage. She jabbed a shaking finger right at Lyra’s nose.

Before Beverly could even start screaming, Genevieve grabbed her arm. Cue the waterworks. She looked so damn fragile. "Lyra, seriously, blame me," she whimpered, her eyes red. "Scream at me, slap me, whatever. Just don't do this to Mom and Dad."

"I spent my whole life as an orphan. I finally have a real family. Please... don't ruin this for Mom. It’s killing me." She let out a pathetic little sniffle, right on cue.

Beverly totally bought it. Her heart practically broke. *See that?* she thought. *That’s the Wynn bloodline for you.* Lost for years, and she was still an angel. Not like Lyra—that ungrateful little bitch. Beverly shot Lyra a look of pure, unadulterated disgust.

Lyra just laughed. A cold, sharp sound. 

Before they could even blink, Lyra lunged forward. *Smack.* Her hand connected with Genevieve’s face in a brutal blur.

The sound cracked like a whip in the quiet room.

Genevieve cupped her burning, red cheek, eyes wide. No way. Did Lyra just... hit her? The same Lyra who used to follow them around like a beaten puppy? Had she lost her mind?

"Lyra!" Beverly shrieked, losing her damn mind. This bitch really just slapped her golden child? Right in front of her? It felt like a slap to her own face. Blind with rage, Beverly wound up and swung hard at Lyra.

Lyra didn't even flinch. She snatched Beverly’s wrist mid-air, locking it down. 

With a brutal twist, she shoved. Beverly went flying backward like a cheap doll, slamming straight into Genevieve. They both stumbled, lost their footing, and hit the floor in a tangled mess.

Lyra stood over them, looking down like they were trash. They groaned on the floor. A wicked, gorgeous smirk spread across her red lips, making her look drop-dead stunning.

"Hey, you're the one who told me to hit you," Lyra mocked. "You want to play the martyr? Fine. I’m just helping you get into character."

Back when Genevieve first showed up, Lyra actually tried. She bent over backward, doing everything to make nice. But Genevieve? She just hid behind that sweet-little-me act, framing Lyra left and right, turning the whole family against her. And Lyra took it. She swallowed the abuse because she actually cared about the Wynns. She didn't want to rock the boat.

Back then, they were everything to her. Now? They were absolute garbage. And Genevieve? She was less than nothing.

"You literally said I could slap you. So shut up and take it," Lyra sneered. "Or was that little speech just a show for Eleanor?"

Genevieve froze, her ugly expression slipping. She squeezed her puffy cheek, looking like a kicked puppy. "No, that's... that's not it. I just didn't want you to—"

"Then shut up and take it," Lyra snapped, cutting her off cold. "Cut the crap. These idiots might buy your little show, but I don't. From now on, you see me, you walk the other way. Don't make me put my hands on you again. Got it?"

###chapter 5
Lyra tossed the strap over her shoulder. She spun around, whipping out her phone. "Yeah, we're good. Pick me up," she said. No drama, just straight-up authority.

Beverly went red. Seeing Lyra stand so tall made her sick, especially remembering how the girl used to beg them for a scrap of attention.

Something snapped inside Beverly. She lost it. "Get the hell out! Go on! Let's see how tough you are when you don't have the Wynn name protecting your ass!"

She scrambled off the floor, grabbed Genevieve by the arm, and hauled her inside, spitting curses the whole way.

Genevieve kept glancing back. Lyra's figure was shrinking down the driveway. Genevieve bit her lip, hard. Who the hell was on the other end of that call?

Mom always said Lyra was just some hick. They only dragged her back to the city four years ago after her grandma kicked the bucket. She was a total fish out of water around rich folks. Her whole life was just the Wynns and Caspian.

But now she was dumped. Who would actually drive out to the Wynn gates for her?

And damn, that voice of hers. She sounded like a freaking CEO.

Genevieve couldn't help herself. She yanked Beverly toward the study. The massive glass window there gave them a perfect view of the front gate.

Down below, a ride tore up the asphalt and screeched to a halt right by Lyra.

No flashy Lambo, no fancy limo. No logos at all. Just a stealthy, matte-black SUV. It looked mean. Sleek, heavy-duty, and impossible to ignore.

The driver's door popped. A guy in black tactical gear hopped out. Huge frame, buzz cut, face carved out of stone, and eyes like a predator. He marched straight to Lyra, moving with the kind of lethal precision you only get from years in the military.

"Boss," he said, snapping to attention. He gave a sharp, military nod. Total respect. His face was a blank mask of pure, unquestioning loyalty.

Lyra just gave a cool nod.

The guy moved fast, opening the back door for her.

She slid inside without a second thought. No looking back, no regrets. She didn't give the Wynn house a single glance.

The door thudded shut, sealing the cabin tight.

The guy jumped back behind the wheel and fired up the engine.

Rubber burned.

The SUV roared and blasted down the road like a rocket.

Up in the study, Genevieve pressed against the glass. She watched the buzz-cut guy usher Lyra in. Even from up here, the guy radiated pure danger.

Right before he climbed back in, he stopped. Like he felt her watching. He snapped his head up and stared straight at her.

That glare.

It felt like a freezing snake wrapping around her throat, choking the air right out of her lungs.

Genevieve went white. Sweat broke out. Her knees turned to jelly, and she hit the floor.

###chapter 6
"Oh my god, Genevieve, what is it?!" Beverly lunged forward, grabbing her. 

Wallace’s head snapped around. 

Then, a roar ripped through the quiet—pure, raw horsepower. A massive black tank of an SUV tore into the driveway. 

Wallace bolted upright. His eyes went wide, tracking the heavy metal beast as it peeled out and vanished. His chest tightened. 

The guy knew cars. His own garage was packed with high-end imports. But this thing? He’d never seen anything like it in his life. 

A cold shiver hit his spine, making him scowl. "Who the hell owns that ride?"

Genevieve buried herself in her mom's side, white-knuckling her dress. Her mouth shook. "Lyra... she just got in."

Wallace stiffened. "Lyra?" 

No way. That wasn't some cheap Uber. How did a girl like Lyra roll with someone who had that kind of cash? And close enough to get a personal pickup at the Wynn gates?

"Ugh, what are you guys even stressing about?" Beverly rolled her eyes. She’d seen the truck, but whatever. "Trash hangs out with trash. Whoever is driving that thing is probably a nobody." 

Besides, she didn't see a logo on the grill. Probably some cheap knockoff brand too embarrassed to show a badge. Why were they losing their minds over this?

A knock rattled the study door. The maid stood there, looking super awkward. "Um, sir? Ma'am? I was just... cleaning Lyra's room. I found these on her vanity." 

She slid a piece of paper and a plastic card onto the mahogany desk.

"Toss it," Beverly snapped, barely glancing at the desk. "Why are you bringing that brat's garbage in here?"

Wallace stared at the card, his forehead creasing. He snatched up the paper. It was covered in Lyra's sharp, elegant cursive. A neat, bulleted list.

Right at the bottom, she’d scrawled a bold, messy note: *[This covers everything I cost you over four years at the Wynn house, rent included. Total: $500,000. PIN is 000000.]*

Wallace’s face darkened. 

Beverly peered over his shoulder and let out a sharp laugh. "Oh, please. Look at her playing accountant." 

She skimmed the numbers. "Half a million? Seriously? That’s Genevieve’s monthly allowance! She lived like a freaking princess here for four years. No way she only spent that much."

"Cheap people stay cheap. I guess her whole life is only worth five hundred grand," she sneered. "And please, even if she wants to play independent, where the hell did she get that kind of cash anyway?"

Wallace didn't answer. He stared at the paper, his eyes turning cold. He could still feel the sting of that $500,000 check she’d slapped right into his face. Her eyes had been ice. She wasn't bluffing.

He read the list again, crumpling the edges of the paper in his fist. "Get the butler," he growled. "I want a full audit. Every single cent, every meal, every scrap of paper Lyra used in this house for the last four years. Now!"

###chapter 7
One look. That’s all it took to read the whole damn page. 

Four years. Lyra lived under the Wynn roof for four whole years, and her entire life’s cost fit on a single, flimsy piece of paper? 

If this leaked, high society would think the Wynns went flat broke. They’d look like cheapskates who starved their own kid.

Wallace stared hard at the plastic card. "Run the numbers on this. Now." 

The butler snatched the card and the paper, scurrying off to double-check.

Beverly opened her mouth to complain, but Wallace’s face looked like thunder. She shut her trap, rolling her eyes. "Seriously? You’re buying this?" she hissed. "The brat is playing hard to get. It’s a total mind game."

"She wants us to feel guilty. She’s begging for pity, trying to make us soft so we crawl back begging."

No way in hell did Lyra only spend half a million in four years. A basic maid cost way more than that. Beverly knew this trick. She’d seen trashy girls play it a thousand times.

***

Meanwhile, inside the SUV. 

Rhys sat stiff, his buzzed head barely moving as his hands gripped the wheel. He shot a quick look in the rearview. In the back, the girl had her eyes shut, totally checked out.

"Yo, Boss," Rhys said, his voice buzzing with hype. "Now that you’re done with the Wynns, we heading straight back to the Gray Zone? The crew’s dying to see you."

Lyra cracked one eyelid. "For now..." she murmured.

Her phone buzzed, cutting her off. An unsaved Vaelion City number flashed on the screen.

She swiped up. A panicked, older guy’s voice blasted through the speaker. "Miss! It's Silas. Your dad sent me to grab you, but—damn, I’m so sorry—I got wrecked on the way to the Wynns. I’m stuck in the ER at Starlight Royal right now."

Lyra squinted. *Miss? Butler?* 

Hold on. The Wynns said her real family lived in some trashy, run-down slum on the edge of Vaelion. Those fancy words didn't scream "ghetto" at all.

"Miss... I really screwed up. I'm so sorry I'm late," Silas groaned, sounding miserable. 

Lyra didn't even blink. "Send the address. I'll drive."

Silas started stammering another apology, trying to spit out the location, when a loud shout cut him off. 

"Hey! Bed one's family! Anyone here for bed one? Her BP is tanking, heart rate is through the roof! We’ve got internal bleeding—get her to the OR, now!"

Silas gasped. He yelled out, "Doctor! Over here! What’s happening to her?"

The doctor sounded grim. "She’s crashing. The scan shows a bleed right next to a main artery. We need to cut her open immediately."

Silas panicked. "Then do it! Save her! I don't care what it costs, just fix her!"

"It’s not a cash issue," the doctor sighed, sounding stressed. "The bleed is in a nasty spot, and her heart is weak. The risk is insane. Honestly? She’s got less than a ten percent shot."

Translation: no doctor wanted to touch this with a ten-foot pole.

Silas’s voice shook, but he tried to hold it together. "This is Starlight Royal! You guys have the best docs in Vaelion! Is there seriously nobody brave enough to do this?"

"Elias, you’re the hotshot surgeon here. You can't do anything?"

Right then, a nurse sprinted over. "We’re losing her! Bed one's BP is still tanking, and her pupils are blown! If we don't move, she’s dead in ten minutes!"

###chapter 8
Clack. The butler dropped his phone. It hit the linoleum. 

Heavy squeaks of sneakers neared, then a frantic whisper cut through the room. "Elias, look. Bed one's chart. I just ran her ID. You won't believe who this girl is..."

A heavy pause. "Seriously, if she dies under our roof, we're done. That man will literally destroy us."

Elias snatched the folder. His eyes went wide, his pupils shrinking to pinpricks. "Where the hell is Edward?" he snapped, panic bleeding into his voice. "He’s the only surgeon in the entire city who can pull off this kind of operation!"

"We called him," the nurse stammered. "He's at some big-shot conference next door. He jumped in his car, but... god, she might flatline before he even hits the city limits."

"We don't have time!" Elias barked. "Look at her—she's turning blue. Her lips, her nails, they're gray. Her stats are cratering!"

"Push an IV bolus of Norman Forte. Now." A sharp, cocky voice sliced through the panic. "Hook up the rapid fluids. We need to stabilize her numbers and buy Edward some time."

The room exhaled. The doctors practically beamed. "Astrid! Thank god. Is Edward right behind you?" 

Elias pressed, stepping forward. "Are these his direct orders, Astrid?"

Astrid was Edward's right hand—the gatekeeper to the city's golden-boy surgeon. She was a powerhouse herself, a regular at global medical summits. Around Starlight Royal, her word was law. 

"Yes, they're Edward's orders," Astrid said, her chin up. "He's flooring it. Until he gets here, we keep her alive. Move!" she snapped at the nearest nurse. "Get on it!"

The nurse scrambled to turn around, nodding like a bobblehead. Then, a chilly, deadpan voice drifted up from the floor. "Do that, and your hospital is getting sued into oblivion."

It wasn't loud, but it hit like a physical wall. The nurse stopped dead. 

Astrid scowled, throwing a dirty look at the phone on the carpet. "Who is that? Ignore them," she told the nurse. "Go. We're running out of minutes."

The butler gasped, finally realizing his call was still active. He snatched the phone up, hands shaking. "M-Miss Lyra..."

"Block her," Lyra's voice cut through the speaker, crystal clear. "No Norman Forte. She's blue because of oxygen deprivation. That drug has Compound Y. You pump that in, you'll trigger a massive allergic reaction right on top of her internal bleeding. She'll be dead in five minutes flat."

Silas didn't blink. He threw his body right in front of the nurse. "Step back. You're not touching her with that."

Astrid sneered, her face twisting. "Are you insane? Think about what you're doing. Does your 'Miss' even have a medical degree? A license? Edward's word is law in this field. Who the hell do you think you are to question him?"

"She's literally dying!" Astrid yelled. "If we don't treat her right now and she flatlines, who takes the fall? Let me make this crystal clear: if you block us, the hospital is completely off the hook for her death."

"I'll take the fall," Silas growled, standing like a brick wall. "My boss said no meds, so you're not touching her. Put it all on me. I'll own whatever happens."

###chapter 9
"You're gonna take the fall? With what cash, Silas?" Olivia's face iced over. "Edward doesn't screw up. Push the meds. Do it now before she dies."

"Seriously!" another white-coat cut in. "Norman Forte doesn't have some BS 'compound Y' in it. An allergy? Please. Stop trying to scare everyone."

"The guy's a freaking legend. His surgeries literally write the textbooks!"

"Inject her! Right damn now!"

Silas lunged to block the syringe.

"Grab him!" Olivia yelled. "He touches anyone else, call 911!"

Two guys pinned Silas. He thrashed, totally helpless. "Miss Lyra! Help! What do I do?"

Lyra didn't even raise her voice. "If they want to play dumb, let 'em. They can clean up their own mess."

Olivia snorted, throwing her weight around. "Push the plunger. Now."

The line exploded into pure static and shouting.

Silas's heavy, desperate grunts echoed through the speaker as he fought the hold.

Then, a hollow gasp. "It's... it's in. They pushed the Norman Forte..."

Lyra kept quiet.

The trainwreck was already playing out in her head.

Boom. Right on cue.

It took, what, three seconds?

"Holy shit! Her throat's closing up! Look at her skin—she's breaking out everywhere! She can't breathe!"

"BP is tanking—I can't get a read! Pulse is down to thirty! We've got V-fib!"

"Anaphylaxis! Oh my god, she's bleeding out and having a massive allergic reaction! What the hell do we do?!"

The ER went dead silent.

Every single thing went down exactly the way Lyra said it would.

Olivia's face drained of color. She started shaking. "No way. No freaking way. Edward's gold standard doesn't fail. How is she allergic?"

"She's defective! Yeah! It's her body's fault!"

She was scrambling for a scapegoat.

But her voice was cracking like glass.

Silas watched the chaotic swarm of doctors trying to revive the kid. He squeezed his phone like a lifeline, betting everything on Lyra. "Miss... you can fix this, right? Tell me you can fix this."

Lyra paused.

This random butler she'd never even laid eyes on had backed her up from second one.

Because of him, she didn't hate the idea of her birth parents quite as much.

"Listen to me," she said, her voice dropping into pure authority. "Find an acupuncturist. Get their needles and gear. Now."

Her chill vibe instantly cut through the panic.

Silas spun and roared at the room. "Get me a Chinese medicine doc! Right now! My lady knows how to save her!"

"Acupuncture? Seriously?" Olivia sneered through her panic. "That's literally just voodoo and placebo."

Silas didn't have a second to waste on her crap.

He locked eyes with Elias. "Find me a traditional doctor. Now! If anything goes south, it's on my head!"

Elias opened his mouth to argue.

Then he caught a glimpse of Silas's collar. It was slightly parted, showing a hidden lapel pin. Elias froze. Color rushed out of his face, sweat popping up on his forehead. He turned and screamed at his team, "Move your asses! Go find one!"

###chapter 10
Talk about a shitshow. 

Two of Vaelion’s heaviest hitters, both dumped in Starlight Royal’s ER at the exact same time. Total, absolute madness.

A nurse dragged a baby-faced resident into the chaos. The girl looked like she was about to puke. "Look, I—I know some basic holistic stuff," she stammered, hands twitching. "But I’m seriously out of my depth here..."

"Just do exactly what I say," Lyra cut in. Her voice was ice-cold, fast, and sharp as a scalpel. "Listen up. [Insert Lyra's unique traditional treatment process]! Got it? You have exactly one hundred and twenty seconds. Move!"

The resident froze. The sheer weight in Lyra's voice snapped her out of her panic. Her brain shut off, and her hands took over, flying through the steps on pure muscle memory.

Olivia balled her fists, her face twisting into a nasty sneer. "Oh, please. A couple of weeds and some pins? She thinks she’s a miracle worker?" Typical Olivia—she’d started this fire, but she still had to throw shade.

The rest of the white-coats chimed in. "Elias, seriously? You’re just gonna let this circus slide?" 

"We need real science here! Prep the paddles! Push the epi, now!" 

"Since when do needles beat high-end imported drugs? Why the hell do we spend billions on pharma research if we're doing voodoo?" 

"Just wait till Edward shows up. You're dead meat."

Then, a gasp. 

The resident yelled, "Holy shit, she’s reacting! The throat swelling is going down! Her airway is clearing!"

"Vitals are climbing! BP is ninety-five over sixty, heart rate's at one-fifteen, O2 is ninety-five! Her lips are turning pink—she’s coming to!"

The room went dead silent.

The island was a giant, roaring torch. Everyone just stared. The rich snobs collapsed onto the deck, faces white as chalk. Some shook like leaves, others bawled their eyes out, and a couple just blacked out cold from the sheer shock.

Lyra stood right at the bow of the speedboat. The ocean wind whipped her hair all over her face. The orange glow of the fire danced across her frozen, gorgeous features. She looked totally blank, but heavy.

Julian slid an arm around her waist, pulling her tight against him. "Hey. Where'd you go?" he muttered.

Lyra stared at the water for a long second. "My nan."

Julian didn't push. He just squeezed her hand.

The flames shrunk into the dark distance. "I always thought she just got old and passed," she whispered, her voice barely carrying over the engine. "It messed with my head for years. I learned all this medical stuff, saved a million strangers, but I couldn't do crap for her."

"But that Obsidian Sun guy... he knew her."

"Her death wasn't some accident."

It had to be them. The Obsidian Sun.

Her knuckles turned white as she balled her hands into fists.

"I don't care how deep they're buried. I'm digging them up and ripping them apart."

***

Vaelion City was pitch black by the time they docked. Julian’s guys were already lined up at the harbor. Lyra hauled herself into the back of a massive, luxury SUV. The warm streetlights flickered through the glass, hitting her tired eyes.

She didn't say a word the whole drive. She just leaned her head back against the leather and shut her eyes.

But Julian knew she wasn't sleeping. The vibe radiating off her was suffocating, heavy with whatever happened to Elara.

The SUV finally rolled up to the Lancaster gates. She reached for the door, but Julian grabbed her wrist, pulling her right back into his chest. He rested his chin on her head, his voice low, thick, and possessive. "Stop thinking. Just go inside and crash, okay?"

Lyra tilted her head up, her face inches from his. His eyes locked onto hers, totally intense, like nothing else in the world existed. It was hot, heavy, and made her feel completely safe.

"I'll deal with the rich snobs from the island," he murmured, a slow, wicked smirk playing on his lips. "And I'll get the cops to sweep up whatever's left of the Obsidian Sun's local crew. If the world ends, babe, your fiancé has got you covered."

"Your only job is to sleep. Got it?"

The tight knot in her chest finally snapped. Warmth rushed through her. She buried her face in his chest and nodded. "Yeah. Okay."

He kissed the top of her head, lingering there. "Go. Your family's waiting."

Lyra blinked up at him. "Wait, how'd you know?"

Julian let out a dry laugh. "Ethan called me like three times already."

A real smile finally broke across her face—the first one since the island blew. "See you later, then."

"Yeah. Get some sleep."

He stood by the car, watching her walk up the steps and disappear inside before he finally turned to leave.

Inside, the Lancaster mansion was lit up like a Christmas tree. Reginald sat stiffly, holding a cup of tea that had gone totally cold. Frederick kept twitching, staring at the front door every two seconds. Eleanor was busy shredding a tissue, and Ethan was practically glued to the window, checking the driveway for the hundredth time.

Then, the maids outside started shouting, "Welcome back, Miss!"

The whole family scrambled, jumping out of their seats and sprinting for the foyer.

Lyra walked through the door, and every eye in the room slammed onto her.

"Lyra..."

They all stared, scanning her from head to toe, looking for blood or bruises. Once they saw she was in one piece, the whole room let out a massive, collective sigh of relief. Lyra stood there, feeling the heavy, thick wave of their love wash right over her.

###chapter 1170
Her throat tightened. "Hey," she whispered, looking at them. "Grandpa. Dad. Mom. Ethan. I'm back."

Eleanor lunged forward, tears spilling over. She grabbed Lyra's hands, squeezing them tight.

"Oh my god, sweetie, you did it! Eleven straight wins! Like, a literal world record!"

"That paper your team dropped? It totally blew the global medical scene away. They finally see what Elyndor can do!"

"Seriously, the top neuro-heads are calling your stuff the biggest breakthrough in ten years!"

Reginald grinned, chest puffed out. "Damn right! That’s my girl!"

They crowded around her, throwing compliments left and right, hyping up her genius.

Nobody asked why she bailed right before the big trophy moment.

Or why she let her team take the spotlight for a historic win.

The Lancasters didn't care about that stuff.

They just wanted her safe, successful, and sitting right here in their living room.

A wave of pure heat bloomed in Lyra's chest. This was real, no-strings-attached love.

She watched them. Suddenly, she was sixteen again. Her dying grandma was clutching her hand, wheezing out: *Just be happy, baby. Get loved. Get cared for.*

Lyra blinked, her eyes stinging with sudden moisture.

She stared at the noisy, loving crowd in front of her.

Then she thought of Julian. His arms around her just minutes ago, so warm and safe.

A real, soft smile tugged at her mouth.

*Hey, Grandma. Look at this city. I think some of these lights are actually mine now.*

"Okay, okay, back off, let her sit," Reginald barked, though he was smiling as he waved everyone to the couches.

Eleanor glued herself to Lyra's side, still holding her hand like she'd disappear.

Lyra took the praise, nodding and smiling.

Eleanor finally patted her knee and headed to the kitchen for the midnight snack she'd whipped up. That's when Lyra looked at Ethan.

"So, Ethan. What's the word on the Wynn Group?"

Ethan snorted, pushing his gold-rimmed glasses up his nose. "Just like you wanted. We tore it down and rebuilt it."

"It's The Afia Group now. Our guys took over the board. Every single asset is cleared, logged, and locked down."

Lyra nodded.

Aria.

Her grandma's name.

That company belonged to her anyway. Those bloodsucking Wynns didn't own a single brick of it anymore.

"As for the family," Ethan continued, "we took it all. The mansions, the rides, the bank accounts. Frozen and seized."

"They spent the last week in Vaelion begging like stray dogs. Looking for cash, loans, anything to get back on top. Obviously, everyone ghosted them."

"Once they realized they were screwed, they crawled back to the sticks. They're crashing in Elara's old, crappy shack right now."

Ethan paused, his voice dropping. "That place was in Elara's name, so I left it alone. Figured you'd want that."

Lyra looked him in the eye. "Thanks, Ethan. Seriously."

She hadn't planned on totally destroying them when she walked away. She wanted to respect her grandma's memory.

She wasn't even going to claw back the money she'd given them.

But the Wynns basically begged to be ruined.

They loved acting high and mighty, looking down on country folks. Now they could rot in the dirt. Poetic justice.
